record.original_question: A general triple plane is a triple cover f: X → P^2 with branch locus B such that f is unramified over P^2 \ B, one has f^*B = 2R + R' with R smooth and irreducible and R' reduced, and the restriction f|_R: R → B is the normalization map of B. Do there exist general triple planes with p_g = q = 0 and Kodaira dimension κ(X) > 0?

evidence.quote: Question: Does there exist general triple planes with pg = q = 0 and Kodaira dimension κ(X) > 0? Examples with Kodaira dimension −∞ and 0 have been provided in [31].

artifact.category_tag: triple covers of the projective plane
artifact.status_search_result: The classification work of Faenzi–Polizzi–Vallès (Trans. AMS, 2019) constructs general triple planes with p_g = q = 0 in families I–VII and produces examples with Kodaira dimension −∞ and 0. No published construction of a general triple plane with p_g = q = 0 and κ > 0 was located, and the question is posed as an open problem in subsequent expositions. Status appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Triple planes with p_g=q=0
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of general triple planes with p_g=q=0 into 12 families; examples constructed for types I–VII.
status_evidence.claim: Existing constructions produce examples of low Kodaira dimension; the higher Kodaira dimension case is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Triple planes with pg=q=0 (Faenzi–Polizzi–Vallès)
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit families of general triple planes with p_g=q=0 are described.
status_evidence.claim: No example with κ>0 is exhibited in the classification.
